For a graded connected algebra and a graded module bounded below, homogeneous generators are equivalent to generators of \(M/\Lambda_+M\); inclusion-minimal generating families correspond to inclusion-minimal spanning families of that quotient. [source-2@L1520-L1533|claim=formal-document]

claims.text: Minimality does not imply that indecomposables are free of the same rank, even for a torsion-free underlying abelian module. Let \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(M=(2,x)\subset R\). Then \(\{2,x\}\) is an inclusion-minimal homogeneous \(R\)-generating family, \(M\) is torsion-free over \(\mathbb Z\), and \[ M/R_+M=M/xM\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2. \]

Minimality also does not determine rational rank. For \(M=R=\mathbb Z[x]\), the homogeneous family \(\{2,3\}\) is inclusion-minimal and generates \(R\), but \[ M/R_+M=R/xR\cong\mathbb Z, \] of rank \(1\), although the family has cardinality \(2\).

If \(M\) is a finite-rank free abelian group and \(N\subseteq M\), then \[ M/N\cong\mathbb Z^N \] holds if and only if \(N\) is saturated in \(M\) and \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl((M\otimes\mathbb Q)/(N\otimes\mathbb Q)\bigr)=N. \]

For the proposed \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), a direct proof must separately establish saturation of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) and the indicated rational dimension; minimality alone cannot provide either conclusion.
